descriptions.text: Tome of Gatekeeper. This is an Advance Reader Copy. Street date: 12th floor. Cost: 75 Mana. Target: Any opponent or NPC or deity or OI entity. Duration: (5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell) × [Your Intelligence / (Target's Constitution + Charisma)] Ahh, Gatekeepers. I hate Gatekeepers. … This spell removes the target's ability to use any skills or abilities associated with their class for a short period. If this spell is cast on a deity, they will temporarily lose access to their Worshipper Base Associated skill and spell set. You probably don't know what that means yet. It's basically most of their spells and skills, but if it's a god made of lava, they'll probably still be able to fuck you up with lava. …

recap.text: Donut makes Carl take her spell book, the Tome of Gatekeeper, from the floor prize, then zaps it into his hand without having read it. It is a paperback, the first Carl has seen, with a drawing of an angry woman standing before a gate on the cover. Its description rants about gatekeepers, then explains itself, and when Carl asks Mordecai what an OI unit is, Mordecai has no clue.

beats.headline: An advance reader copy
beats.text: Donut insisted on claiming her spell book from the floor prize, and she has not read it yet: she thinks it is a good spell, but she is not allowed to use it, and its duration is in nerd math. She zaps it into Carl's hand. It is, strangely, a paperback, the first he has seen, and looks nothing like a spell book, with a drawing on the cover of an angry woman standing in front of a gate. Its description rants about gatekeepers for a while and then explains itself. Carl asks Mordecai what an OI unit is. Mordecai has no clue.
beats.gist: Donut zaps her unread spell book to Carl, a paperback showing an angry woman before a gate.
